scope: Installs persistent Strix host monitoring, captures the first observed model-read I/O failure and spontaneous reboot, and records NVMe SMART/controller health. This does not repair the host or prove the source artifact readable.

deployment.retention: 720 hourly event files, 512 MiB aggregate cap

failure_sequence.journal_recovery: systemd-journald reported system and user journal files corrupted or uncleanly shut down
failure_sequence.interpretation: An approximately 43 GiB sequential read preceded the failed hash and abrupt reboot. The prior-boot kernel journal contains no persisted NVMe or EXT4 error before ending, so the reset or storage-path hang outran journal persistence.

watcher_design_correction.initial_probe: The first watcher implementation invoked nvidia-smi; that command entered an uninterruptible state and outlived Python's 8-second subprocess timeout.
watcher_design_correction.correction: The persistent watcher never invokes nvidia-smi. It reads /proc/driver/nvidia and filters journald NVRM/Xid/driver-mismatch messages. The service uses KillMode=process so a blocked helper cannot own the watcher lifecycle.

nvme_smart.historical_short_self_test: completed without error at power-on hour 17471
nvme_smart.historical_extended_self_test: completed without error at power-on hour 491

checks.name: watcher-unit-tests
checks.result: 5 tests passed: disk/network rates, journal filtering, bounded event rotation, process-state parsing, and persistent non-nvidia-smi service contract.

checks.name: selected-setup-gate
checks.result: All ten selected setup/tool test modules passed.

checks.name: remote-service
checks.result: Active and enabled after the observed reboot; latest state had zero D-state processes and active SSH/journald/networkd/ZeroTier services.

checks.name: smart-and-controller-logs
checks.result: SMART passed with zero media errors and zero controller error-log entries.

non_claims: SMART health does not refute the observed Linux I/O error or sudden reboot; it indicates no current NAND-media or controller error counter.
The failure mechanism is unidentified. PCIe/link, power, firmware, kernel, filesystem, thermal, or controller instability remain possible.
No new SMART self-test was started because an extended test would add substantial read pressure to a host that reset during a 43 GiB read.
The 92 GB source GGUF was not retried after the I/O error and must not be treated as readable.
No standard iMatrix rerun was launched on Strix after the failure.
The watcher's journal cursor cannot recover kernel lines that were never persisted before an abrupt reset.
